_comment: The approval authority for Dockerfile base/tool image pins (#349). Every digest-pinned image reference in any Dockerfile must appear here with the exact same image, tag and digest, and every pin row must still be referenced by at least one Dockerfile -- the registry and the tree hold each other closed, so a base update is always a reviewable change to this file plus the Dockerfiles. A pin reference is `name:tag@sha256:<digest>`: the digest is the resolution authority (immutable), the tag is the human-readable version annotation. All digests below are the manifest-list (index) digests the named tag resolved to on `recorded`, so every architecture/platform variant of that tag is fixed by one pin and a fixed target platform always resolves to the same per-arch artifact. Checked by scripts/check-image-pins.py, which also rejects any `:latest` reference and any unexempted unpinned base. `exemptions` exist for INTERNAL images that intentionally keep a version tag; each must name an owner, an issue and a reason, exactly like quality/image-inventory.json's coverage exceptions -- an exemption nobody owns is just an exemption.

pins.note: CPython 3.13.18 on Debian bookworm-slim; the interpreter pin that keeps coincurve building from source only on purpose. Refreshed from 3.13.16 (#1152 lineage, this #2303 CI repair): the grype leg of the container gate flags CPython binary HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs whose fixes landed in the next point release -- this refresh moves for CVE-2026-115557 (CRITICAL in the 3.13.16 binary, fixed 3.13.18), the same mechanism as #363's CVE-2026-19445/19553/82049 move to 3.13.16. The in-image and security.yml identity smokes assert (3, 13, 18) so the exact-patch contract moves with the pin; scripts/smoke-engine-canvas.sh's canvas-less CONTROL_IMAGE shares this exact pin (held closed by tests/test_pinned_digest_references.py); digest re-resolved by pulling the tag on 2026-11-16 and reading the interpreter version from the image itself.

CPython 3.12.x line as of the recording date (resolves to 3.12.16); research, RSI runner, e2e and sbx-tests images. Refreshed (#363): the grype leg of the container gate flags CPython binary HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs fixed in the next point release -- this refresh moves the tag from the 3.12.15 digest to the 3.12.16 one for CVE-2026-115557 (CRITICAL, grype --only-fixed), same advisory that drove the 3.13.18-slim-bookworm row. Digest refreshed 2026-10-24 (#93) for the libbrotli1 cache-chain repair: security.yml runs 40081082641/40088232144/40091186336 flag libbrotli1 1.1.0-2+b7 (CVE-2026-111497, HIGH, fixed 1.1.0-2+deb13u1 / DSA-6582-1) in maistro-rsi-runner even though the same runs' build logs show the re-executed apt stage installing 1.1.0-2+deb13u1 -- buildx cache keys are computed pre-execution from the instruction string and parent key chain, never from a RUN's fresh bytes, so `--no-cache-filter runtime-apt` re-executes the stage but cannot stop the downstream stages from reusing pre-advisory cache chains (and mode=max cached manifests) that carry the old OS layer into the loaded image. The base-digest bump changes the key chain from the FROM down, so the rebuilt image assembles the freshly executed layers (same doctrine as the 3.13.x refreshes).
Copier template base: rendered downstream images pin the identical digest.

Builds the age static binaries and the static docker CLI from their pinned upstream release tags (#363, then #1152): the published docker:29-cli binary embeds go1.26.8 stdlib and the age prebuilt binary go1.25.x, both carrying 2026 stdlib HIGHs (CVE-2026-78667/78669/97031, fixed in go1.26.9/1.27.2) that no released tag of either project ships fixed. The 1.27.2 rebuild then aged out itself: CVE-2026-111943 (crypto/x509 MITM via untrusted intermediate certificates, HIGH, fixed in go1.26.10/1.27.3) flagged both binaries' stdlib, so the builder moved to 1.27.3-alpine — #1095's trunk-CI repair independently hit the same advisory and re-resolved the same tag to this identical digest. Resolved 2026-10-22 hours after upstream re-serialized the tag's index with unchanged per-arch content (the earlier same-day index d530cf60723abf1ffae0cd16bb546b379ec0550d2f3815e5b16ed69dbc00fba4 carries the identical linux/amd64 child). The same 1.27.2 -> 1.27.3 bump was independently required by the #795 container-cache repair lane, whose Container scan gate flagged the identical CVE on the age/age-keygen and docker CLI binaries.

uv 0.12.21, verified by running `uv --version` from the image the :latest tag resolved to on the recording date; the tag was rewritten from :latest to the release it actually was. The API image and the Conductor image join this list with #348: both now install their Python dependency set from the committed uv.lock through this pinned uv, so the installer that resolves the shipped set is itself immutable.

Playwright browsers + deps, e2e harness only. The #2303 refresh is a real content move, not an index re-serialization: the tag's per-arch manifests changed (linux/amd64 bdfda2a8 -> d65108d1, linux/arm64 68456172 -> 969a9e36) because Microsoft rebuilt the same v1.64.1-noble tag on 2026-10-23 (previous image created 2026-10-14). Both configs still report Ubuntu 24.04, the same PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH env and 7 layers, and the harness pins its own `@playwright/test@1.64.1` at build time, so only the base OS/browser layers moved.
